title: Mouse cursor stays locked / captured even after hitting a breakpoint with an IDE like Rider on certain Linux systems
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproduced in v4.3.stable.mono.official [77dcf97d8]
- IDE Used: JetBrains Rider 2024.3.5
- Windowing System: X11
- GNOME Version: 42.9
- OS: PopOS 22.04 LTS

### System information

Pop!_OS 22.04 LTS - X11 - GNOME 42.9 - Godot v4.3.stable.mono.official [77dcf97d8]

### Issue description

After hitting a breakpoint inside a C# script with an IDE such as JetBrains Rider, if the game had the mouse captured (as most games do), the mouse cursor will still be tied and captured to the now unresponsive game window, even if it was running in Windowed mode. The only way to get the mouse cursor back, is to halt the debugging process with a shortcut (such as Shift + F5), making breakpoints much more difficult to use since one cannot see or even interact with the mouse cursor during that time.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new C# script and attach it to a node
2. Set the mouse mode to be 'captured'
3. Set up a breakpoint that will be hit during runtime

At that point the game window is unresponsive, and the mouse cursor is still unavailable.

When a breakpoint is hit, the mouse cursor should be released automatically, allowing interaction with other windows or debugging tools.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mousecaptureproblem.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18717789/mousecaptureproblem.zip)

Please remember to set a breakpoint on the first Console.WriteLine in the project!
